_note: LABELLED SAMPLE: a made-up script about how an AI video editor reuses assets, to show the plan format and how techniques are picked from meaning. Times ('t') are seconds because this sample has no EDL; a real film uses 'words' [first, last] from edl.json.

passages.text: Hi, I'm Alex. My editor finishes a video in fifteen minutes now.
passages.goal: Know who's talking and why this is worth watching
passages.why: names the speaker on the speaker, no title card

beats.show: name title rises; the speaker stays full frame (W)

passages.text: The first video took me two days. Then the whole project was gone.
passages.goal: Feel the cost of starting from zero every time
passages.why: a human consequence lands faster acted out than told

beats.show: stickman types at a desk, Day 1 -> Day 2
screen goes blank: hands on head, then facepalm

passages.text: Every video goes through the same five steps: record, clean up, plan, find motion, build.
passages.goal: See the whole workflow as five ordered steps
passages.why: an ordered process; the same diagram returns for the recap

beats.show: five nodes reveal left to right as he names them

passages.text: The trick is the cache. Anything made once - an asset, an animation, an effect - is saved and picked up next time.
passages.goal: Understand what the cache stores and where it sits in the flow
passages.why: the mechanism lives between two steps; zooming into the same diagram keeps the context

beats.show: camera focuses 'Find motion'; note 'from the cache'

passages.text: Here's the registry on GitHub: every scene has a template, a version and a fallback.
passages.goal: See the real registry and where the version and fallback live
passages.why: the real screen proves it; zoom + highlight show exactly where to look

beats.show: recording plays; zoom into the template list
highlight 'fallback' with a label; cursor clicks it

passages.text: In code it's four lines: get the template, check the ratio, use the fallback if needed, render from the cache.
passages.goal: See the selection logic as real code
passages.why: four real lines; highlighting the ratio check carries the point

beats.show: highlight the ratio check: 'wrong ratio -> fallback'; the cache line is added (diff)

passages.text: Render it, and the checks run automatically.
passages.goal: Trust that every render is checked
passages.why: real command, real output (numbers from a real run)

passages.text: Compared with a timeline editor, nothing is redone by hand.
passages.goal: Weigh the old way against the new way, point by point
passages.why: aligned rows let the viewer compare each point directly

passages.text: So: record, clean up, plan, find, build - and every step gets faster.
passages.why: the recap is the same diagram, now all ticked

beats.show: the workflow diagram returns at overview; steps tick one by one

passages.text: Comment 'repo' and I'll send you the link.
passages.goal: Know exactly what to do next

beats.show: end card with the CTA and handle
